(a) **Rate Constant & Units:**
Rate constant ($$k$$) is the proportionality constant in the rate equation representing the reaction rate when concentrations of reactants are unity.
* Unit of second-order rate constant: $$\text{L} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1} \cdot \text{s}^{-1}$$ (or $$\text{m}^3 \cdot \text{mol}^{-1} \cdot \text{s}^{-1}$$).

(b) **Arrhenius Equation Calculation:**
Given: $$k_1 = 5000 \text{ s}^{-1}$$, $$T_1 = 25+273 = 298 \text{ K}$$, $$E_a = 6 \times 10^4 \text{ J}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$$, $$k_2 = 10000 \text{ s}^{-1}$$.
Using the Arrhenius relation:
$$\ln\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{R} \left(\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right)$$
$$\ln(2) = \frac{60000}{8.314} \left(\frac{T_2 - 298}{298 T_2}\right)$$
Solving yields $$T_2 \approx 307.15 \text{ K}$$ (or $$34.15 \;^{\circ}\text{C}$$).

(c) **Physisorption vs Chemisorption:**
| Feature | Physisorption | Chemisorption |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Forces | Van der Waals forces | Chemical bonds |
| Heat of adsorption | Low ($$20-40 \text{ kJ/mol}$$) | High ($$80-400 \text{ kJ/mol}$$) |
| Reversibility | Reversible | Irreversible |
| Temperature | Decreases with rising temp | Increases initially with temp |

(d) **Michaelis-Menten Equation Derivation:**
Consider the enzyme reaction mechanism:
$$E + S \underset{k_{-1}}{\overset{k_1}{\rightleftharpoons}} ES \xrightarrow{k_2} E + P$$
Using the Steady-State Approximation (SSA) for the intermediate complex $$ES$$:
$$\frac{d[ES]}{dt} = k_1[E][S] - k_{-1}[ES] - k_2[ES] = 0$$
$$\text{Thus, } k_1([E]_0 - [ES])[S] = (k_{-1} + k_2)[ES]$$
Defining the Michaelis constant $$K_m = \frac{k_{-1} + k_2}{k_1}$$, we get:
$$[ES] = \frac{[E]_0[S]}{K_m + [S]}$$
The reaction rate $$v = k_2[ES]$$. Since maximum velocity $$V_{\max} = k_2[E]_0$$:
$$v = \frac{V_{\max}[S]}{K_m + [S]}$$
proTip: For the Michaelis-Menten derivation, always clearly state the Steady-State Approximation ($$d[ES]/dt = 0$$) and substitute total enzyme concentration $$[E]_0 = [E] + [ES]$$.
